turns.text: The previous story examined Actor-Critic. Now the camera turns to A3C and a new question along the same timeline: Why did researchers need A3C, and where were the existing methods getting stuck?

Deep reinforcement learning systems often relied on large replay buffers and specialized hardware to stabilize correlated experience. A3C explored whether many lightweight agents acting in parallel could provide diverse updates without replay.

Multiple worker agents interact with separate environment copies and asynchronously update shared actor and critic parameters. Advantage estimates reduce variance by comparing observed returns with the critic baseline.

Experts generally view A3C as an influential demonstration that asynchronous actor-critic training could be simple, stable, and broadly applicable. It helped popularize advantage-based policy optimization and parallel environment sampling.
The thread continues with SARSA, where researchers push the problem one step further.
